title: Particle-in-a-box residuals and identifiability exercise
status_detail: Completed as a calculated illustrative finite-dimensional experiment selected by the human on 2026-08-20 and extended by explicit human requests while preserving convergence studies. A retained protocol now maps every Appendix D requirement to evidence, and experiment-level Markdown and standalone LuaLaTeX provisional Appendix D reports integrate the derivation, convergence, norm, and identifiability results; the LaTeX source compiles locally with all retained graphics. Results cover the N=8, M=3 three-residual construction; all declared N=8,16,32,64,128,256 convergence, full-spectrum, and multi-norm sweeps; and an executable retained-space identifiability demonstration. Independent verification passes the residual identities, fixed-mode convergence, analytical dispersion, nodal sine-vector overlap, multi-norm oracles, scaled algebraic residuals, two distinct exact decompositions of the same reduced Hamiltonian, and Frobenius fits to scalar, diagonal, tridiagonal, and unrestricted real-symmetric model classes. The convergence studies remain supporting numerical evidence; the identifiability result directly resolves Appendix D's central point that reference-operator and admissible-model-class choices precede physical interpretation. This is numerical verification for the stated finite constructions only; the illustrative alternative has no physical assignment, and aligned operator convergence, continuum interpolation accuracy, software API acceptance, semiconductor evidence, scientific validation, UQ, external execution, and successor activation are not claimed.
objective: Develop the particle-in-a-box exercise that distinguishes continuum domains, finite-difference representation, spectral retention, boundary realizations, and inequivalent residual operators.
authorized_scope: Plan closed-form and illustrative finite-matrix checks for the Dirichlet box and its second-order finite-difference representation.
Represent full-space and retained-coordinate operators explicitly and distinguish consistently compressed, unmatched-compression, and boundary-realization residuals.
Use the exercise to identify minimum state-space, domain, projection, embedding, and model-class information without freezing a public scientific API.
completion_criteria: The analytical identities and finite-matrix constructions agree under explicit domains, bases, dimensions, and embeddings.
The three residual constructions are executable and cannot be conflated by their result representation or documentation.
Verification is labeled analytical or numerical as applicable, and no semiconductor or scientific-validation claim is made.
exclusions: No DFT, Wannier localization, material model, impurity interpretation, external execution, or public API stabilization is in scope.
A reduced Hamiltonian alone is not treated as identifying a unique kinetic-potential decomposition.
Completion does not automatically activate another exercise.
